catalog_quote: Word stress in Liŋŋit̯iɣ is predictable: the first vowel which is preceded by a consonant is stressed. Accordingly, the first vowel is stressed in words beginning in a consonant or cluster -- kápan short, ŋgóðRo black -- but the second vowel in words which begin in a vowel -- ayóŋ I, alán sky, aðá crow.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable that has an onset consonant: word-initial syllable in consonant- or cluster-initial words, second syllable in vowel-initial words (the onsetless initial vowel is never stressed). Historically this is the Northern Paman shift of stress from the Proto-Paman initial syllable to the second syllable, with loss of *C1 (fascicle pp.167-168).
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned; rule stated as exceptionless ('predictable'). Hale flags the segment inventory (not the stress rule) as 'extremely tentative'; data from ~2 weeks' fieldwork with one speaker (Sam Kerindun), 1960.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for the word ('word stress'); examples are isolated citation forms including an inflected pronoun (ayóŋ 'I'). Intonation/terminal pause contours treated separately in the next paragraph.
new_statements.identity_note: Hale's sketch describes Liŋŋit̯iɣ (Linngithigh proper) as recorded from one speaker, Sam Kerindun, at Aurukun in 1960; Hale states Linngithigh and Alngith (Alŋit̯, glottocode alng1239) 'are dialects of a single language, sharing 87 percent of basic vocabulary', but the stress statement and examples are Linngithigh only. Matches leni1238 directly.

sources.note: p.179: word stress is predictable -- the first vowel preceded by a consonant is stressed: first vowel in consonant/cluster-initial words (kápan 'short', ŋgóδRo 'black'), second vowel in vowel-initial words (ayóŋ 'I', alán 'sky', aδá 'crow'). Also p.167-168 (Paman group section): Northern Paman initial-syllable reduction is associated with a shift of primary stress from the initial to the second syllable.
